title: Adaptive prompt segmentation for inter-request KV sharing and memory compaction
creator: Amelia Park
description: Problem: Prefix/prompt fragments reused across user requests are an opportunity to avoid re-populating KV cache on the GPU, but naive global deduplication either uses too much CPU/host RAM or causes contention on the per-GPU allocator. We need a low-latency, memory-efficient approach that finds commonly repeating prefix segments across requests and materializes them into shared, compacted GPU slabs.
context_and_goals: We want a mechanism that: 1) identifies repeated prompt fragments across user requests with bounded CPU cost, 2) stores materialized KV rows in compact slab regions on GPU memory for reuse across concurrent sessions, 3) minimizes allocator fragmentation and eviction churn, 4) preserves latency SLOs for tail requests. Success criteria include >=10% end-to-end token-cost reduction for typical chat workloads and <=5% median latency regression relative to current baseline when feature is enabled for canary customers.
acceptance_criteria: Detect repeated prompt segments at the prefix level with a probabilistic fingerprint (<=0.1% false positive rate) without per-request deep comparisons
Materialize shared KV fragments into 'hot' and 'warm' slab pools on GPU with a per-GPU slab allocator, reducing duplicated KV allocation across concurrent requests
Expose runtime toggles and telemetry so we can safely roll out: cache_hit_rate, per-shard collision_count, eviction_rate, median_latency, p95_latency
No data leakage between customers: prefix-level keys must be namespaced by tenant; private deployments must respect VPC/airgapped constraints
Rollback disables shared slabs and gracefully falls back to current per-request KV materialization with no request failures
tasks: Prototype lightweight 64-bit rolling fingerprint with sampled token windows on host (Diego)
Design and implement per-GPU slab allocator with hot/warm/cold tiers (Eng Slab Team)
Implement namespaced cache keys to maintain tenant isolation and optional masking for private deployments (Security review)
Integrate detection into continuous-batching path to emit reuse hints without blocking fast-path token generation
Add metrics and dashboards for hit-rate, collisions, eviction churn, latency percentiles
Canary rollout to <5% traffic behind feature flag; monitor and iterate
notes: 2026-02-25 - Amelia Park: Created ticket after infra + product sync. Initial idea: avoid per-request KV duplication by materializing common prefix fragments into shared GPU slabs. Scoped down to prompt segments rather than entire prompts to keep memory bounded.

2026-03-02 - Diego Mendez: PoC complete for rolling fingerprint. Uses sampled windows of 32 tokens (every 16 tokens) and a 64-bit XorShift-derived fingerprint. False positive rate measured ~0.07% on production traces (sampled). CPU overhead ~0.9% at 200 RPS per host.

2026-03-05 - Performance review: PoC integrated with host allocator reduces duplicated KV bytes by ~18% for chat workload A, but caused slight increase in p95 due to rare slab contention when many async materializations occur. Plan: add async materialization queue with backpressure and limit concurrent slab writes per GPU.

2026-03-09 - Security: Namespacing proposal reviewed. Must include tenant id and an ephemeral prefix salt to avoid cross-tenant fingerprint collisions. Private deployments flag to disable telemetry leaving only on-host deterministic dedupe.

2026-03-11 - QA: Added tests for collision handling; when collision_count per-day exceeds threshold, system disables sampled-window dedupe for that shard and falls back. Also added a metric 'dedupe_disabled_reasons' for observability.

2026-03-12 - Diego Mendez: Kickoff work on slab allocator. Implemented a compacted slab format where KV rows are stored contiguously in 64B-aligned chunks. Eviction hint vector added so GC can evict cold segments with minimal scanning. Starting canary instrumentation next week.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Fingerprint collisions could cause incorrect reuse across different prompts. Mitigation: namespace by tenant id + ephemeral salt and track collision_count; disable dedupe on high collision rate.
Risk: Slab allocator fragmentation leads to out-of-memory. Mitigation: implement compaction pass and maintain hot/warm/cold tiers with size thresholding and proactive eviction.
Risk: Materialization I/O creates latency spikes. Mitigation: perform materialization asynchronously with bounded concurrency and defer low-priority materializations behind the fast-path.
Risk: Security/compliance concerns in Private deployments. Mitigation: offer a config to disable remote telemetry and run dedupe deterministically on-host with no shared control-plane state.
rollout_plan: Start with internal canary (infra/dev) -> 1% customer traffic (opt-in) -> 5% canary bucket with active monitoring -> broaden after 2 stable weeks. Feature flag gates: sampling_rate, hot_slab_size, concurrent_materializers. If p95 latency increases >5% or collision_count spikes, rollback flag flips and all shared slabs are disabled.
rollback_plan: Toggle off feature flag, drain async materializers, evict shared slabs and ensure per-request KV population resumes. Provide a migration utility to flush potential stale slab references.
